learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the basic concepts of production and manufacturing systems, metrology, and quality control.

Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems related to production and manufacturing systems, metrology, and quality control using established methods.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of product, process, and method engineering.
Understanding of the different methods of production and manufacturing systems and the ability to use them.
Technical and laboratory competencies in production and manufacturing systems.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems related to production and manufacturing systems, metrology, and quality control.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in production and manufacturing systems, metrology, and quality control, and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of engineering products, processes and methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competencies.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Measurement techniques, metrology, and quality control.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final exam (60% weight, practical content) requires a minimum of 4 points out of 10. Laboratory practices are compulsory and require attendance, completion, and a 'PASS' grade. For the extraordinary call, a minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required on the final exam. The final grade will be the maximum of: (Continuous assessment (40%) + Final exam (60%)) OR (Final exam (100%)). For the theoretical part of the extraordinary final exam, students with an average of 5 points or more in partial exams may skip it, receiving the maximum of their final exam theory grade or partial exam average as their theory grade. The problem part of the extraordinary final exam requires a minimum of 3.5 points out of 10.
